speaker: penny
text: I just love decorating the Christmas tree. It makes me feel like a little girl again.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: We didn't have a tree when I was growing up.

speaker: penny
text: Really? Why not?

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Mmm, in my family, holidays weren't so much celebrated as studied for their anthropological and psychological implications on human society.

speaker: penny
text: Oh, sounds festive. Did you at least give presents?

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Mmm, in a way. We presented papers, and then broke off into focus groups and critiqued each other.

speaker: penny
text: Sheldon, what about you? Did you have a Christmas tree?

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Oh, yes. We had a tree, we had a manger, we had an inflatable Santa Claus with plastic reindeer on the front lawn. And to make things even more jolly, there were so many blinking lights on the house they induced neighbourhood-wide seizures.

speaker: penny
text: So I take it you don't want to help us trim the tree.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: I do not. But if you insist on decorating a spider-infested fire hazard in my home I would request that you add this.

speaker: penny
text: What is it?

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: You're kidding, right? It's a bust of Sir Isaac Newton.

speaker: penny
text: Oh, sure, sure, yeah. Very Christmassy.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Wait, excuse me, but it's much more Christmassy than anything you've put on the tree.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Here we go.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: December 25, 1642, Julian calendar, Sir Isaac Newton is born. Jesus, on the other hand, was actually born in the summer. His birthday was moved to coincide with a traditional pagan holiday that celebrated the winter solstice with lit fires and slaughtered goats. Which, frankly, sounds like more fun than 12 hours of church with my mother followed by a fruitcake.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Merry Newton-mas, everyone.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: I sense that's not sincere, although I have no idea why.

speaker: penny
text: No, it's fine. Look, Sir Isaac can go right next to this little candy cane.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: No. Isaac goes at the top of the tree.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: No, he doesn't.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: I understand. You dispute Newton's claim that he invented calculus and you want to put Gottfried Leibniz on the top.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Yeah, you got me. I'm a Leibniz man.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Well, perhaps when your mother gets here, she'll talk some sense into you.

speaker: penny
text: What? Your... your mother's coming? When?

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Tomorrow.

speaker: penny
text: When were you going to tell me?

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Um, tomorrow?

speaker: penny
text: Why were you keeping this a secret?

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Well, I just, I thought...

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: If I can interject here, obviously Leonard is concerned that his mother won't approve of you as his mate.

speaker: penny
text: Why wouldn't she approve of me? I'm adorable.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: You are, it's just...

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: If I can interject again. Leonard comes from a remarkably high-achieving family, who have all chosen high-achieving partners. He probably feels that it's doubtful that his mother will be overly impressed with his dating a woman whose most significant achievement is memorizing the Cheesecake Factory menu.

speaker: penny
text: Hey, it's a big menu. There's two pages just for desserts.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: I know. And those specials, they change every day.

speaker: penny
text: Okay, you know what? It's lame when I say it, it's just ridiculous when you pile on. So what did she say when you told her we were going out? You didn't tell her we were going out, did you? Why not?

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Okay, sorry.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Um...

text: Um...
